headline: Firmus has withdrawn its planned IPO, reported at $5 billion
body: Firmus, an Australian AI data center operator backed by Nvidia, has withdrawn its planned IPO. The company said the proposed offering terms did not adequately reflect its business strength and long-term growth outlook, and it will instead pursue private funding options. Firmus had reportedly sought to raise $5 billion through the IPO, which would have valued the company at about $30.6 billion.
note: Firmus cited market volatility and says it will seek private capital while keeping other public and private options open. Investors judging the next wave of AI listings will watch whether others follow.

evidence.text: "Firmus will now pursue capital from the private markets and consider alternative public and private market options," it added.

Australian AI data center operator Firmus, which is backed by Nvidia , has withdrawn its planned mega initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, the company said in an emailed statement to CNBC.

Australian AI data center operator Firmus, which is backed by Nvidia , has withdrawn its planned mega initial public offering, citing market volatility and conditions, the company said in an emailed statement to CNBC.
The company said the proposed offering terms did not adequately reflect its business strength and long-term growth outlook, and it will instead pursue private funding options.
Firmus had reportedly sought to raise $5 billion through the IPO, which would have valued the company at about $30.6 billion, nearly triple its valuation in August.
